import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_bmi_processed.csv')
df.head()

# Filter the data to include only Hispanic men
hispanic_men = df[(df['GENDER'] == 'MALE') & (df['HISPANIC'] == 1)]

# Display the first few rows of the filtered data
hispanic_men.head()

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for regression
X = hispanic_men[['DISSAVED', 'SAMESAVE']].values  # Predictor variables
y = hispanic_men['BMI'].values  # Response variable

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients
coefficients = model.coef_
coefficients

import statsmodels.api as sm

# Add a constant to the predictor variables
X = sm.add_constant(hispanic_men[['DISSAVED', 'SAMESAVE']])

# Fit the model using statsmodels for detailed statistical output
model = sm.OLS(y, X).fit()

# Display the summary of the model
model.summary()

from scipy.stats import ttest_1samp
import numpy as np

# Extract the coefficients and standard errors from the model
coefficients = model.params
std_errors = model.bse

# Calculate t-statistics and p-values for each coefficient
t_statistics = coefficients / std_errors
p_values = 2 * (1 - ttest_1samp(np.abs(t_statistics), 0).pvalue)

p_values

from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

# Prepare the data for regression
X = hispanic_men[['DISSAVED', 'SAMESAVE']].values
y = hispanic_men['BMI'].values

# Add a constant to the predictor variables
X = np.hstack([np.ones((X.shape[0], 1)), X])

# Create a linear regression model
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

# Get the coefficients and standard errors (approximated)
coefficients = model.coef_
std_errors = np.std(model.predict(X) - y) / np.sqrt(X.shape[0])

# Calculate t-statistics and p-values for each coefficient
t_statistics = coefficients / std_errors
p_values = 2 * (1 - np.abs(t_statistics))

p_values
